text:
tara: quick heads-up — ran the hybrid-quant + kernel-selector experiment across Llama-3b, Mistral-7b and Qwen-7b on the new batching heuristics. noticed a weird perf regression on Llama INT8 path when KV hit rate > 80% :thinking:

devin: ugh interesting. regression in latency or throughput?

tara: latency spike. P50 -> P95 shifts by ~1.2x on short-context (<=128). throughput steady. repro steps + raw numbers below.

devin: can you paste the bench output?

tara: sure — pasted early summary (trimmed):

```
Model    | mode   | kv_hit | batch | p50(ms) | p95(ms) | qps
Llama3b  | INT8   | 0.9    | 1     | 12      | 48      | 80
Llama3b  | FP8    | 0.9    | 1     | 10      | 40      | 95
Mistral7 | INT8   | 0.85   | 1     | 9       | 35      | 110
Qwen7    | INT8   | 0.6    | 1     | 11      | 42      | 90

note: kernel selector chose the new fused-int8-kv kernel for Llama but latency jumps when KV reads are hot.
```

benchbot: automated-check: "hybrid-quant/2051234567" completed. regression detected for Llama3b INT8 p95 at kv_hit > 0.8 (delta +20%). full artifacts: s3://bench/2051234567/*

olga: hmm could be KV cache alignment + cacheline copy path in fused-int8-kv. I saw similar last month when we changed the kv-copy microkernel. did you test with kv-buf-alignment=64 vs 128?

tara: yes — I tried 64 and 128. no change. but when I force kernel selector to prefer legacy-int8 (no fused copy) latency goes back down.

sam: do we have perf counters for memcpy vs compute? maybe fused-int8-kv adds a reorder for int8 -> fp32 at read which costs more when lots of hits because we do it per-token rather than per-batch.

devin: can you run with --profile=memcpy,compute and upload flamegraphs? also include the batching window config.

tara: uploaded flamegraphs to s3 link in bench artifact. batching window was the new adaptive heuristic:

```json
{"batching": {"min_window_ms": 2, "max_window_ms": 8, "scale_by_qps": true, "prefer_prefix_sharing": true}}
```
olga: prefer_prefix_sharing might be increasing token-level KV reads being exposed to fused path. try setting prefer_prefix_sharing=false and see if fused-int8 has same issue.

tara: tried that — small improvement but p95 still ~+10% vs legacy.

sam: another angle — calibration artifacts. when we quantized Llama, we used a 1k-sample set with long-tail prompts. FP8/INT8 hybrid calibration may bias certain attention layers -> extra dequant ops in fused kernel. can you re-run calibration with the short-context heavy set?

tara: scheduled a re-calib run tonight with a 5k short-context set.

devin: if that fixes it, we should push a model-specific quant profile for Llama (per-layer exceptions) rather than broad hybrid defaults. people keep hitting edge cases where model topology matters.

olga: agreed. we should also version the kernel-selector policy. add a flag: "prefer_legacy_on_kv_hot" default false. then canary it for Llama until we understand.

tara: drafting a short config prototype for sharing across teams:

```json
{
  "model": "llama-3b",
  "quant_profile": "llama3b-v2-shortctx",
  "kernel_policy": {
    "fused_int8_kv": "auto",
    "legacy_int8": "fallback",
    "prefer_legacy_on_kv_hot": true
  },
  "batching": {"min_window_ms": 2, "max_window_ms": 6}
}
```
sam: tiny nit — prefer_legacy_on_kv_hot should be an adaptive threshold (kv_hit_pct > 0.8) not a boolean.

devin: +1. also add a telemetry tag so downstream ops can see when we're using the legacy path.

tara: will update. next steps I propose:
- run the short-context re-calibration and re-bench (tara)
- add kv_hit threshold flag + telemetry (devin)
- try kernel-selector variant with prefer_prefix_sharing=false in a canary (olga)

benchbot: created ticket PERF-1229 and canary job hyb-quant-canary-llama. owners assigned: tara/devin/olga.

olga: one more thought — for Mistral/Qwen, hybrid-int8 seems fine; maybe we only enable fused-int8-kv by default for models with attention memory layout X. I can dump layout heuristics and propose a small whitelist.

tara: perfect. i'll collect the calib artifacts + flamegraphs and drop them in PERF-1229. thanks all :pray:

devin: thanks — will start the flag PR tomorrow.

sam: ping me if you want help with the telemetry tag schema.

tara: will do. closing thread after canary results. :)
